externalAnchors.use: Official film page for the 1992 screen continuity and quadrupedal adult xenomorph anchor.
Licensed articulated Dog Alien sculpt; the product page confirms a long body, extendable inner mouth and bendable tail.

projectIdentityReference.note: The V56 board controls the low, long runner proportions and black-russet project palette. It is not proof of a published external Dust Runner model.

designLock: One extremely low and long adult quadrupedal xenomorph adapted for dusty terrain: smooth eyeless elongated skull, compact barrel ribcage, long forelimbs for sprinting, powerful digitigrade hind legs, four readable supports, double jaw and one long blade-tipped segmented tail. No dorsal tubes. Worn wet black and dark russet biomechanical shell with irregular matte ochre sand deposits, never a uniform yellow recolor. No equipment, armor, wings, rider horns or metal plates.

sourceContract.matte: perfectly flat solid #FF00FF, no shadow, scenery, gradient, texture or checkerboard
sourceContract.cellIsolation: one complete subject per cell with blank gutters; no anatomy crosses a cell boundary

limitations: Dust Runner is not an attested Alien 3 or Aliens: Crucible model name; no 1:1 canon claim is allowed.
External pages were studied as design anchors only. No official bitmap, texture, sculpt photograph or unpublished Crucible concept is copied into the deliverable.
Generated boards remain source candidates until extraction, pose chronology, identity, scale, root and loop review pass; no automatic runtime acceptance or integration.
The selected opaque backgrounds are normalizer-compatible magenta but are not pixel-uniform #FF00FF; exact matte replacement/removal belongs to a separately authorized normalization step.
